facts.fact: ISO's member register entry lists The Gambia Standards Bureau (TGSB) as the country's ISO Correspondent member, whose purpose is to standardize methods, processes and products, with standards development and sales among its services; the page carries no date, so its published date 2026-09-03 is used, and it names no law and no standard on information technology or data.

note: No fact on certification: the page lists inspection, testing and certification as a service but names no IT or data standard and no certifier or certified body.

facts.fact: The Point reports the TGSB Director General saying the Bureau was established under the Gambia Standards Bureau Act in 2010 and now has more than 70 staff after absorbing the former Weights and Measures Department; the article is dated 2026-07-01 and the establishment date is the event.

note: The Director General's claim of about 500 standards developed, harmonised and adopted names none on information technology or data, so it is no fact on published; no certification is mentioned; the Legal Metrology Act 2025, ARSO membership and organic standards are non-IT and not facts.

facts.fact: The Gambia Standards Bureau was established by an Act of Parliament in 2010 (TGSB Act 2010) to develop and publish national standards in all sectors, and also to provide conformity assessment and metrology services, according to the bureau's own 2022 catalogue.

The bureau's 2022 catalogue of national standards lists GAMS ISO/IEC 27001:2005, Information Technology - Security Techniques - Information Security Management Systems - Requirements (ICS 35.030, 41 pages), as a Gambian Standard adopted from ISO; the catalogue's abbreviations define GAMS ISO as adopted ISO standards, and the catalogue is dated 2022 on its cover.

systems.owner: Government of The Gambia (statutory body under the TGSB Act 2010; appointed WTO TBT Enquiry Point in 2014 by the Ministry of Trade, Industry, Regional Integration and Employment)

note: No certification fact: the catalogue lists product certification and system certification among the bureau's services but names no certificate issued against an IT or data standard, no certifier accredited in the country and no certified organisation; ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and other non-IT entries are class other and place nothing.
Only SPS standards bodies are rated, not IT or data standards.
States nothing on national IT standards for this country.
